lines: Clock divider with eight outputs, each dividing the clock by a number taken from a table of integers, even numbers, odd numbers, primes, powers of two, random chances or an eight-step rotation
Advances the count on a rising edge, reading high at 1V and low again at 0.5V
A rising edge sets the count back to zero, so every output begins its cycle again
Picks the table of division numbers: integers 2 to 9, even 2 to 16, odd 3 to 17, primes 2 to 19, binary 2 to 256, random, or an eight-step rotation
Carries 10V when the count reaches the number printed against it; in random mode it fires with a chance of one in that number, and in sequential mode on its own step of an eight-step rotation
Each press steps the output shape on: gate holds until the next clock, trig gives a 1ms pulse, gate2 holds for half the division cycle, and as is copies the pulse width of the clock
Musical fires each output on the first clock of its division cycle and math on the last; the random and sequential tables are unaffected by it
Note — Nothing runs on its own: every output stays at 0V until the first rising edge arrives at the clock input, and the count begins from that edge
HolonicSystems-Gaps.notes: TRIG_MODE_PARAM (param 1) holds the output shape but has no widget, so it cannot be clicked; the LED button (param 2) cycles it and carries the line. The four shapes are gate, trig, gate2 and as is, although the parameter is configured with a maximum of 2.

lines: Two independent 32-step recorders, each capturing a CV and a gate on every clock and looping them back, polyphonic to sixteen channels
Advances both recorders by one step on a rising edge; recording and the outputs move only on this edge
A rising edge sets both recorders back to their first step
Records the CV and gate inputs of that side for one full loop length, then stops on its own
A rising edge records the CV and gate inputs of that side for one full loop length, then stops on its own
Records the CV and gate inputs of that side over the existing loop for as long as it is held down
Records the CV and gate inputs of that side over the existing loop while this gate is high, reading high at 1V and low again at 0.5V
Erases the CV and gate of all 32 steps of that side, on every polyphonic channel, the moment it is pressed rather than on a clock
A rising edge erases the CV and gate of all 32 steps of that side, on every polyphonic channel
The CV recorded into that side; its channel count, or the gate input's, sets how many polyphonic channels are recorded and played back
The gate recorded into that side, stored as whatever voltage is present when the clock arrives
Sets the loop length of that side in steps, a reading of 0 giving one step and 31 the longest the knob reaches
Lengthens the loop of that side by one step per volt, added to the length knob, with 32 steps the limit
Moves the play and record position of that side through the 32-step buffer, 0 to 31 steps
Moves the play and record position of that side on by one step per volt, added to the shift knob
The recorded CV of that side at the current step, renewed on each clock
The recorded gate of that side at the current step, renewed on each clock
Note — Both recorders move only on a rising edge at the clock input, so with nothing patched there the outputs never change, and nothing is recorded however the record buttons are used
Note — A side plays back as many polyphonic channels as are patched to its cv and gate inputs at that moment, so unpatching them leaves its outputs carrying nothing
HolonicSystems-Pantry.notes: The installed 2.0.7 build configures the length knobs 0 to 31 and the combined length is clamped to 1 to 32, so a knob reading of 0 gives a one-step loop. The maker's next commit changes the range to 1 to 32 and also corrects the tooltip spellings Lenth and Lengh.

lines: Eight-step sequencer and addressable switch: a clock, or a voltage, picks one of eight inputs and sends it on to the CV output
The voltage this step passes to the CV output; with nothing patched the step passes a fixed 10V
Scales what this step passes to the CV output, from nothing through to full level
Off, or a 1ms 10V pulse on the first or the second trigger output each time the sequencer reaches this step
A rising edge moves the sequencer on one step, in the direction the mode knob sets
A rising edge jumps the sequencer to the step the start knob sets
Selects a step directly, 0-10V spanning the steps from the start knob over the set length; with a cable in the clock input it is read only on a clock edge
Attenuates the address input, narrowing how far across the steps 0-10V reaches
Picks how the sequencer moves: forward, backward, pendulum, or a random step on each clock
Adds to the mode knob, 0-10V spanning the four ways of moving and wrapping round at the end
Nothing in the module reads this control; the mode input is added to the mode knob at full level
Sets which of the eight steps the sequence starts from
Shifts the starting step, 0-10V spanning all eight steps, added to the start knob and wrapping round
Attenuates the start input, narrowing how far 0-10V shifts the starting step
Sets how many steps the sequence runs before it returns to the start, one to eight
Adds to the length knob, 0-10V spanning eight steps and wrapping round at eight
Attenuates the length input, narrowing how far 0-10V lengthens the sequence
Attenuates the CV output, from nothing through to full level
The selected step's voltage, scaled by that step's own attenuator and by the output attenuator
A 1ms 10V pulse each time the sequencer reaches a step whose switch is set to 1
A 1ms 10V pulse each time the sequencer reaches a step whose switch is set to 2
Sequencer holds the selected step's voltage until the sequencer moves on; switch passes the selected input continuously, so a changing input is heard between steps
Note — In sequencer mode the CV output stays at 0V until the step changes, so a clock, an address voltage or a reset is needed before anything comes out
Note — In switch mode the selected step's voltage is passed continuously from the moment the module is placed, with no clock needed
HolonicSystems-DumbwaiterSequencer.notes: Mode CV Att (param 23) is on the panel and can be turned, and the process function never reads it: the MODE input is added to the mode knob unattenuated. Change Trigger (output 3) is declared and given a tooltip name but has no jack on the panel and is never written to, so it gets no line.

lines: Four channels of CV shaping, each with an inverter, an attenuator, a sample and hold, a VCA, a low-pass filter, a slew limiter, an offset and AC coupling
The voltage that channel shapes; with nothing patched the channel starts from 0V
A rising edge samples that channel's input and holds it until the next edge; with nothing patched the input passes through unheld
Sets the gain of that channel: 0V silences it, 5V passes it unchanged and 10V doubles it; with nothing patched the channel passes at full level
Flips the sign of that channel's input before anything else in the channel
Attenuates that channel's input, from nothing through to full level
Bends the VCA response of that channel, exponential fully counter-clockwise and linear fully clockwise
Fully counter-clockwise the channel passes unfiltered; turning clockwise lowers the cutoff of the low-pass filter
Sets how slowly the channel climbs towards a rising input, 10000V per second fully counter-clockwise and 0.1V per second fully clockwise
Sets how slowly the channel falls towards a dropping input, 10000V per second fully counter-clockwise and 0.1V per second fully clockwise
Bends the slew shape of that channel: fully clockwise gives a constant rate, and turning counter-clockwise slows the approach as the output nears the input
Adds a fixed -5V to 5V to that channel after the slew limiter
AC strips any steady voltage out of the output with a very slow averaging filter; DC leaves the output as it is
The finished first channel, clamped to -10V to 10V
The finished channel, clamped to -10V to 10V, with the output of the channel before it added in whenever that channel's own jack is empty
HolonicSystems-SwissCheeseKnife.notes: The order along a channel is invert, attenuate, sample and hold, VCA, low-pass filter, slew, offset, AC coupling. The VCA response knob crossfades between an exponential curve and a linear one; the maker's comment marks it as unfinished, but the crossfade is applied.

lines: Turns OSC messages from the Holon.ist iOS app, or from any OSC sender on the network, into eight control voltages
Picks which of the eight OSC buses, A to H, this module reads; a second copy set to another bus gives another eight channels
A rising edge renews every output whose s/h switch is on; outputs with the switch off are unaffected
Attenuates the value arriving on that channel, from nothing through to full level
Fully counter-clockwise the channel passes each arriving value at once; turning clockwise smooths the jump from one value to the next
On, that channel's output is renewed only on a rising edge at the clock input; with nothing patched to that input the output follows the incoming values continuously
The voltage for that channel, clipped to -10V to 10V, with its lamp green for positive and red for negative
Multiplies arriving CV values by ten, so a value sent in the range -1 to 1 becomes -10V to 10V; gates, triggers and the app's own LFO shapes are unchanged by it
Note — OSC arrives on UDP port 9000, and the module advertises itself over Bonjour so that Holon.ist finds it; the app also sends the channel names printed against the outputs
Note — The outputs stay at 0V until an OSC sender reaches the module and sends on the bus the bus knob has selected; the lamp beside a channel flashes when a value arrives on it
HolonicSystems-HolonicSource.notes: The ten-fold scaling from the osc input switch is applied only to channels whose incoming mode is unipolar or bipolar CV; gate, trigger, flip-flop, random and LFO channels are generated at fixed levels, 5V for a gate or trigger and -5V to 5V for an LFO shape.

lines: Two independent switches, each passing one of its two inputs to its own output under voltage control
Chooses which of that channel's two inputs reaches its output, reading high at 1V and low again at 0.5V
Reaches that channel's output while the switch is on A, which in gate mode is while the CV input is low
Reaches that channel's output while the switch is on B, which in gate mode is while the CV input is high
Carries whichever of that channel's two inputs the switch has selected
Gate selects the A input while the CV input is low and the B input while it is high; trig flips from one input to the other on each rising edge and leaves it there
HolonicSystems-Junctions.notes: The A, B and output jacks carry whatever is patched through them, audio as readily as CV, so they are given no family.

lines: Four quantisers sharing seven twelve-note scales that can be edited by hand and are saved with the patch
Picks which of the seven scales the quantisers use; the seven start out as the modes of the major scale on C, from Ionian through to Locrian
Steps through the seven scales, 0-10V spanning all of them, added to the scale knob
Attenuates the scale input, narrowing how many scales 0-10V steps through
Shifts the pitch by a volt per octave, before or after quantising as the pre and post switch sets
Pre adds the transpose input to the incoming CV before quantising; post adds it to the quantised pitch, rounded to whole semitones
Attenuates the CV input of all four quantisers before they round it to a note
Turns that note on or off in the scale the scale knob has selected, and its lamp is lit while the note is on
The voltage that quantiser rounds to the nearest note of the scale, carrying up to sixteen polyphonic channels
A rising edge takes a fresh reading of that quantiser's CV input; with nothing patched the quantiser follows its input continuously
The quantised pitch of that channel, a volt per octave
A 1ms 10V pulse each time the quantised pitch of that channel changes to a new note
HolonicSystems-LazySusanQuantiser.notes: The twelve note buttons edit whichever of the seven scales is currently selected, so the scale knob and the scale input both change what a button press affects. Edited scales are stored in the patch under the key scales.
